summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of mitochondrial myopathy, autonomic dysfunction, and coronary artery disease was admitted after increasing his metoprolol dose from 25 mg to 50 mg, leading to lightheadedness, diaphoresis, and a significant systolic blood pressure drop. He reported ongoing difficulty staying hydrated despite oral intake, attributed to possible malabsorption. Evaluation ruled out acute cardiac events with normal troponins and non-specific EKG changes. Chest X-ray showed no acute cardiopulmonary issues. He was treated with IV fluids, which resolved his symptoms and improved renal function. Medication changes included discontinuation of isosorbide mononitrate due to side effects and switching from esomeprazole to famotidine. Metoprolol was reduced back to 25 mg twice daily. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to maintain hydration, continue adjusted medications, and follow up with primary care and gastroenterology for malabsorption evaluation.
